summary: The current revision satisfies the visible fresh-state path: public rendering is record-free, every public access control opens the truthful local prepared-workspace gateway, pricing has exactly the approved Pilot and Network plans, workspace switching and reset use one reducer, matched screenshots preserve the locked design, and commit-bound verification remains fresh because later commits change only verification evidence and task status. Release readiness is blocked by the unchanged version-3 persistence contract: browser state saved by the pre-ACCESS application is accepted as current, allowing the retired record-bearing SIGN_IN screen or the prior Maria scenario to survive deployment and bypass the reviewed Camila entry path.

findings.description: ACCESS changes the prepared identity and public gateway but leaves both the existing `oncoready_workflow_state_v2` key and `WorkflowState.version` value 3 unchanged. The baseline at c099646 already stored version-3 Maria state and could persist `currentPerspective: SIGN_IN`; `loadSavedWorkflowState` accepts any parsed object with version 3 and a patient. An existing browser can therefore reload directly into PortalAuthScreen, which exposes record details and bypasses the single truthful gateway, or open the new gateway and then enter the stale Maria workspace. This violates the public record exclusion, one-gateway, prepared-persona, and repeatable recording-path requirements even though clean-storage tests pass.
findings.recommendation: Version or migrate the persisted scenario contract so pre-ACCESS version-3 state cannot be treated as the reviewed Camila scenario. Validate the full persisted discriminator/shape, normalize retired SIGN_IN state to the public landing/gateway path, and add a regression that seeds the pre-change version-3 state (plus a malformed same-version state) before reload and confirms the record-free Camila start.
